about: Where each engine on the page comes from. Each entry names the result rows it covers (impls: '<source>/<name>', as the merged data has them), how the engine is obtained (package: a label and a link), its source (a link) and how the page's runs call it (how: one or two sentences, the same for every engine: the interface, the encodings, the flags and how matches are counted). site/generate_site.py lists the engines of the data at the foot of the page, with the versions the run reported; an engine the data has and this file does not is listed without links, and the build says so.

engines.name: Corvus.Regex.Ecma262
engines.how: Its interpreter over a string (UTF-16), and its source generator over a string and over UTF-8 bytes, with the workload's flags and u, counted with Count.

engines.name: System.Text.RegularExpressions
engines.how: Its interpreter (RegexOptions.None) and its source generator ([GeneratedRegex]), with the workload's options as dotnet/performance gives them, counted with Count.

engines.name: V8 (Irregexp)
engines.how: Node.js 24's RegExp, with the workload's flags and g and u, its matches counted by a loop that advances lastIndex as matchAll does. The answers of the test data are V8's.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262
engines.how: The crate over a &str (UTF-8) and over UTF-16 code units, with the workload's flags and u.

engines.name: regex
engines.how: The regex crate, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags.

engines.name: regress
engines.how: The regress crate, with the workload's flags and u.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262 (C library)
engines.how: The C library through its header, over UTF-8 and over UTF-16, with the workload's flags and u.

engines.name: QuickJS libregexp (quickjs-ng)
engines.how: QuickJS's libregexp, with the workload's flags and u, over the text as QuickJS holds a string: 8-bit when every character is Latin-1, UTF-16 otherwise.

engines.name: PCRE2
engines.how: PCRE2 with its JIT, in UTF mode, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262-cpp
engines.how: The C++ header over UTF-8 and over UTF-16, with the workload's flags and u, its global search made once per text and walked as a range.

engines.name: std::regex (libstdc++)
engines.how: libstdc++'s std::regex with its ECMAScript grammar (ECMA-262's 3rd edition, as the C++ standard modifies it), over the UTF-8 bytes, with the workload's flags.

engines.name: Boost.Regex
engines.how: Boost.Regex's Perl syntax (its ECMAScript option is the same syntax), over the UTF-8 bytes, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags.

engines.name: SRELL
engines.how: SRELL over the text as UTF-8, with the workload's flags.

engines.name: RE2
engines.how: RE2 with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262 (Python)
engines.how: The package over a str and over UTF-8 bytes, with the workload's flags and u, its matches counted with finditer.

engines.name: re
engines.how: Python's re, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, its matches counted with finditer.

engines.name: regex
engines.how: The regex package, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, its matches counted with finditer.

engines.name: corvus_regex_ecma262
engines.how: The gem over a UTF-8 String and over a UTF-16LE String, with the workload's flags and u, each match taken with each_match.

engines.name: Regexp (Onigmo)
engines.how: Ruby's Regexp, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i and s flags (s as Ruby's m), each match taken with String#scan.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262 (PHP extension)
engines.how: The extension over a string (UTF-8) and over UTF-16 text, with the workload's flags and u, counted with Regex::countMatches.

engines.name: PCRE (preg_*)
engines.how: PHP's PCRE functions in UTF mode, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, counted with preg_match_all.

engines.name: CorvusRegexEcma262
engines.how: The package over a String (UTF-8) and over [UInt16], with the workload's flags and u, counted with matchCount.

engines.name: NSRegularExpression
engines.how: Foundation's NSRegularExpression (ICU), with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, counted with numberOfMatches, which on Linux copies the String into UTF-16 for ICU on every call, so each figure includes that copy.

engines.name: Swift Regex
engines.how: Swift's Regex, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, counting matches(of:).

engines.name: corvusregexecma262
engines.how: The package, with the workload's flags and u, counted with ecma_count over the pattern compiled once.

engines.name: PCRE2 (gregexpr, perl = TRUE)
engines.how: Base R's gregexpr with perl = TRUE and useBytes = TRUE (PCRE2), given the pattern in each call as R programs use it, headed by (*UTF) so that PCRE2 matches characters while R reports byte offsets, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags.

engines.name: TRE (gregexpr)
engines.how: Base R's gregexpr without perl (TRE, which has no m or s flag), given the pattern in each call, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i flag.

engines.name: ICU (stringi)
engines.how: stringi's stri_count_regex (ICU), given the pattern in each call, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262 (Fortran)
engines.how: The binding over a character variable (UTF-8) and over an integer(int16) array (UTF-16), with the workload's flags and u, counted with regex_t%count.

engines.name: POSIX regex (glibc)
engines.how: glibc's POSIX regex (regcomp and regexec, extended syntax, through ISO_C_BINDING), with REG_ICASE for i and REG_NEWLINE for m, searching on after every match.

engines.name: fortran-regex
engines.how: fortran-regex (a port of tiny-regex-c), searching on after every match.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262 for Java
engines.how: The library over UTF-8 bytes (Utf8Text) and over a String (UTF-16), with the workload's flags and u, counted with Matches.count; each again in a JVM started with --add-modules jdk.incubator.vector, where it searches with the Vector API.

engines.name: java.util.regex
engines.how: Pattern over a String, with the workload's flags as Pattern's (i as CASE_INSENSITIVE and UNICODE_CASE, m as MULTILINE, s as DOTALL), counted by a loop of Matcher.find.

engines.name: TRegex
engines.how: GraalJS's RegExp, whose engine is TRegex, run by GraalVM's Node.js with the workload's flags and g and u, its matches counted by the same loop as V8's.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262 for Go
engines.how: The module over UTF-8 bytes (a Text, checked once) and over []uint16 (UTF-16), with the workload's flags and u, counted with Matches.Count.

engines.name: regexp
engines.how: Go's regexp over a []byte, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags as (?ims), its matches counted with FindAllIndex.

engines.name: goja
engines.how: goja's RegExp (a JavaScript engine written in Go), with the workload's flags and g and u, its matches counted by the same loop as V8's.

engines.name: CorvusRegexECMA262.jl
engines.how: The package over UTF-8 (a Utf8Text, checked once) and over a Vector{UInt16} (UTF-16), with the workload's flags and u, counted with count.

engines.name: Base.Regex
engines.how: Julia's Regex (PCRE2 with its JIT) over a String, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, its matches counted with count.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262-pas
engines.how: The library over UTF-8 (a TUtf8Text, checked once) and over a UnicodeString (UTF-16), with the workload's flags and u, counted with Count.

engines.name: TRegExpr
engines.how: Free Pascal's TRegExpr in its two builds: the RegExpr unit over the bytes of the UTF-8 text, and the uRegExpr unit over its UTF-16, each with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, its matches counted by Exec and ExecNext.

engines.name: corvus-regex-ecma262-ocaml
engines.how: The library over UTF-8 (a utf8_text, checked once) and over a string of UTF-16LE, with the workload's flags and u, counted with count_text and count_utf16.

engines.name: re (ocaml-re)
engines.how: ocaml-re through its Perl syntax, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, its matches counted by a loop of searches that goes on one character past an empty match.

engines.name: pcre2 (OCaml binding)
engines.how: The OCaml binding to PCRE2, which offers no JIT, in UTF mode, with the pattern as it is and the workload's i, m and s flags, the text checked as UTF-8 once and not at each search, its matches counted by a loop of searches.
